player_action: I just dropped to exactly 0 hit points. I'm unconscious and start making death saves, right?
game_state: PC took damage leaving exactly 0 hp.
correct_ruling: At exactly 0 hp the character is disabled, not unconscious. He may take a single move or standard action each turn; taking a standard action (or other strenuous action) deals 1 point of damage and drops him to -1 and dying. 3.5 has no death saving throws.
srd_reference: CombatI.rtf > Injury and Death > Disabled (0 Hit Points)
common_wrong_rulings: Unconscious at 0 hp with 5e-style death saves.

player_action: The orc drops my character to -4. What happens each round?
game_state: PC at -4 hp, no healing nearby.
correct_ruling: At -1 to -9 the character is dying: unconscious, and each round has a 10% chance to become stable; otherwise he loses 1 hit point. At -10 he is dead.
srd_reference: CombatI.rtf > Injury and Death > Dying (-1 to -9 Hit Points)

player_action: I'm at -9 and the troll hits me for 3 more. I'm at -12, but I have a Con of 18, so I've got some room left, right?
game_state: Fighter, Con 18, reduced to -12 hp. Core SRD rules.
correct_ruling: No. In the core SRD a character dies at -10 hit points regardless of Constitution. At -12 he is dead.
srd_reference: CombatI.rtf > Injury and Death > Dead (-10 Hit Points or Lower)
common_wrong_rulings: Death at negative Con score (a popular house rule).

player_action: I'm disabled at 0 hp. I cast cure light wounds on myself.
game_state: Cleric at exactly 0 hp casts cure light wounds (standard action) on self.
correct_ruling: Casting is a standard (strenuous) action, which costs 1 hp after the action is completed. However, if the action increases his hit points, as a cure spell does, he is no longer at risk: he heals and is no longer disabled.
srd_reference: CombatI.rtf > Injury and Death > Disabled (0 Hit Points)
common_wrong_rulings: He can't cast at all while disabled.
He drops to -1 before the healing applies and is dying.
confidence_note: SRD says a disabled character who performs a strenuous action takes 1 damage 'unless the action increased the disabled character's hit points'. Ruling follows that; verify exact wording.

player_action: I'm prone. I shoot my longbow at the goblin.
game_state: Ranger lying prone, armed with longbow.
correct_ruling: A prone character can't use a ranged weapon except a crossbow. He must stand (a move action that provokes attacks of opportunity) or switch to a crossbow.

player_action: The archer across the room shoots at the prone kobold. Any modifier?
correct_ruling: A prone defender gets +4 to AC against ranged attacks (and -4 AC against melee attacks). The archer's shot is harder.
srd_reference: AbilitiesandConditions.rtf > Conditions > Prone; CombatII.rtf > Combat Modifiers
common_wrong_rulings: Ranged attacks get +4 against prone targets.
Ranged attacks have disadvantage (5e) with no AC change.

player_action: I stand up from prone and then attack the ogre next to me.
game_state: Fighter prone adjacent to an ogre with reach; fighter's turn.
correct_ruling: Standing up from prone is a move action that provokes attacks of opportunity, so the ogre gets an AoO. The fighter can then take a standard action (a single attack), not a full attack.
srd_reference: CombatII.rtf > Actions in Combat > Move Actions > Stand Up
common_wrong_rulings: Standing is free and he can full attack.

player_action: It's the first round of combat and the bandits haven't acted yet. Can the bandit leader make an attack of opportunity on my rogue when she runs past?
game_state: Bandit leader hasn't acted yet this combat (flat-footed), no Combat Reflexes.
correct_ruling: No. A flat-footed character can't make attacks of opportunity unless he has the Combat Reflexes feat. He also loses his Dex bonus to AC.
common_wrong_rulings: Yes, AoOs work regardless of initiative.

player_action: The monk stuns the wizard. What can the wizard do and what does it mean for us?
game_state: Wizard stunned for 1 round, holding a staff.
correct_ruling: A stunned creature drops everything held, can't take actions, takes a -2 penalty to AC, and loses its Dexterity bonus to AC.
common_wrong_rulings: It can still move but not attack.

player_action: The goblin is dazed. That means it's flat-footed and I get sneak attack, right?
game_state: Goblin dazed for 1 round; rogue adjacent, no flanking.
correct_ruling: No. A dazed creature can take no actions but has no penalty to AC and keeps its Dex bonus. Daze alone doesn't enable sneak attack.
common_wrong_rulings: Dazed is the same as stunned.

player_action: The guard is asleep. I deliver a coup de grace with my dagger.
game_state: Sleeping guard (helpless), rogue adjacent with dagger; guard has no crit immunity.
correct_ruling: Coup de grace is a full-round action that automatically hits and scores a critical hit; the rogue adds sneak attack. If the guard survives the damage he must make a Fortitude save (DC 10 + damage dealt) or die. It provokes attacks of opportunity from threatening opponents.
srd_reference: CombatII.rtf > Special Attacks > Coup de Grace

player_action: The zombie is paralyzed by my hold spell somehow. I coup de grace it.
game_state: Helpless zombie (undead, immune to critical hits).
correct_ruling: You can't deliver a coup de grace to a creature that is immune to critical hits. Undead are immune to crits, so no coup de grace; you'd simply attack normally (helpless target: +4 melee bonus, Dex 0).
srd_reference: CombatII.rtf > Special Attacks > Coup de Grace
common_wrong_rulings: Coup de grace kills it automatically.
It's fine but no extra crit damage.

player_action: I shoot my crossbow at the sleeping guard 30 feet away to coup de grace him.
correct_ruling: You can use a bow or crossbow for a coup de grace only if you are adjacent to the target. At 30 feet, it's just a normal ranged attack against a helpless target.
srd_reference: CombatII.rtf > Special Attacks > Coup de Grace
common_wrong_rulings: Yes, any weapon at any range.
Only melee weapons can ever coup de grace.

player_action: I'm already shaken from the dragon's frightful presence. Now the necromancer casts cause fear on me and I fail. What am I?
game_state: PC is shaken; fails save vs cause fear (frightened).
correct_ruling: Fear effects stack: a shaken character who is made frightened becomes panicked.
common_wrong_rulings: He's just frightened; the worse condition overrides.

player_action: Two different effects make me shaken. Is that -4 on everything?
game_state: PC already shaken, gets shaken again by another effect.
correct_ruling: No. Fear conditions are cumulative but not by adding penalties: a shaken character made shaken again becomes frightened.
common_wrong_rulings: No change; same condition doesn't stack.

player_action: What does shaken do to me?
correct_ruling: Shaken gives a -2 penalty on attack rolls, saving throws, skill checks, and ability checks.

player_action: I'm panicked but cornered with nowhere to run. Can I fight back?
game_state: Panicked fighter cornered in a dead-end.
correct_ruling: A panicked creature drops anything it holds and flees; if cornered, it cowers and does not attack. It can use special abilities, including spells, to flee. It takes -2 on saves, skill and ability checks.

player_action: I'm frightened. Can I cast dimension door to get away?
correct_ruling: Yes. A frightened creature flees from the source of fear as best it can and can use special abilities, including spells, to flee. Dimension door away is legitimate.
common_wrong_rulings: Frightened creatures must move on foot.
